subject: Halo Systems — Redwood integration technical probe

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@halosys.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Halo Systems — Redwood integration technical validation request

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for taking this — excited to explore a technical validation with Redwood. Halo Systems builds a conversational orchestration layer that routes prompts and context to multiple LLM backends. We have a production customer that wants Redwood as a recommended inference runtime (Dedicated or Private) to take advantage of your latency and reliability SLAs.

High‑level asks for the validation:
- Confirm that Redwood can host/serve our adapter (we run a small adapter service that proxies requests and manages session state).
- Validate throughput at 200 RPS average, p95 latency <= 120ms for 2k token context in Dedicated or Private mode.
- Review security requirements — we need SOC2 evidence, TLS mutual auth support, and an approach for restricting KV cache persistence.
- A reference architecture diagram for a Private deployment and a short test matrix so our ops team can coordinate.

Would you have 30–45 min this week for a kickoff? If helpful I can send the reference diagram and a list of test prompts.

Best,
Emily Zhao
Head of Integrations, Halo Systems
emily.zhao@halosys.com
+1 (415) 555‑0127

--
Halo Systems — orchestration for multi‑model CX

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear summary.

We'd love to run a hands‑on validation. Quick answers and next steps:

- Kickoff: I can do 11/19 10:00–10:45 PT or 11/20 14:00–14:45 PT; what works for your team?
- For throughput verification we'll collaborate across Redwood SE and infra (cc'd). Marissa will draft a test matrix and required artifacts.
- Can you confirm the typical model family and peak input size (e.g., Llama 2 70B, 2k tokens, or an ensemble)? Also whether adapter runs inline (same pod) or as an external proxy — this will affect our sizing guidance.
- Security: please attach the SOC2 report and any specific KMS/HSM requirements; we have Private deployment options and can map to HIPAA/SOC controls.

If you can share the reference diagram and a short prompt set before the kickoff that will help Marissa and infra size a Dedicated pool for the smoke tests.

Thanks — looping Sergio to help with partner ops and Marissa to own validation.

Aditya / team — attaching the reference diagram and our privacy/security requirements doc. Answers inline:

- Model family: Primarily Llama‑Large family (70B float or quantized), sometimes smaller 13B for lower‑cost flows. Adapter: our adapter runs as an external proxy service (separate container) that performs session stitching and per‑request routing.
- Peak/expected load: typical production flow is 100–250 RPS (bursty). Most sessions average 1.6k tokens, peak 2k.
- Security: we require TLS mutual auth to the adapter, granular audit logs for prompt/response pairs (retention 90 days), and the ability to disable persistent KV cache for PII flows. SOC2 report attached; we can add an NDA if required.

We prefer a Private validation on a small staging VPC to mirror customer constraints. Proposed kickoff: 11/20 14:00 PT.

From: Emily
--
Emily Zhao
Head of Integrations, Halo Systems

Thanks Emily — this is helpful. I put together a first‑pass test matrix (attached) that covers:
- Functional: adapter handshake, TLS mTLS end‑to‑end, prompt routing correctness, KV cache toggles.
- Perf: steady‑state RPS ramps (50/100/200), p95 latency at 2k context, GPU utilization and token‑per‑GPU metrics.
- Reliability: simulated backend failures, model fallback to smaller variant, and failover across AZs.

Immediate asks from our side before kickoff:
1) Staging endpoint for the adapter + a short health check URL (we'll use the endpoint to smoke the handshake and mTLS).
2) A sample prompt set (10–20 prompts) including a mix of short and 2k‑token prompts and a couple annotated PII cases (so we can validate KV cache behavior).
3) Confirmation you can share read‑only logs for the 90‑day retention check or a sanitized sample.

I'll bring infra leads to the kickoff to confirm Dedicated vs Private sizing if we see high burst behavior. Happy to run the first smoke within 48 hours of receiving staging details.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
